objections.claim: The spec's load-bearing claim (§1) is that "the brand types flow `producer-auth` → `commissaire` across a real production edge, and a mis-typed value … becomes a compile error on the production path." But the ratified `ledger-read-fields-stay-plain-string` resolution forces every ledger-sourced `producer_id`/`contract_revision` to plain `string`, and the verify path must pass those plain strings to `deriveKey` "byte-for-byte as today" with no re-mint. That means `deriveKey`'s `producerId`/`contractRevision` parameters **cannot** be typed `ProducerId`/`ContractRevisionId` — doing so makes `verifyAuthLeg` fail `tsc` (S4a), and the forbidden alternative is re-minting. So the only `producer-auth` API parameters that could carry the brands are the validators' own `unknown` inputs (which accept anything) and their return types. S2 then has no parameter "into the producer-auth API where a `ProducerId` is required" to aim a raw string at: the fixture as specified has no target. The brand is minted by `asProducerId` and immediately erased into a JSON write — it constrains no cross-module edge at all, and the §1 "structural fix" rationale is hollow as specified.
objections.evidence: §1 "Load-bearing model" vs §3 "Ledger-read fields stay plain `string`" ("the verify path passes those plain `string` fields to `deriveKey` unchanged") vs S2 ("passes a raw string at the admission/mint call into the `producer-auth` API where a `ProducerId` is required") vs DONE ("a raw `string` passed to a `ProducerId`/`ContractRevisionId` parameter is a `tsc` error").
objections.predicted_consequence: The holdout S2 cannot be built against the named API; the builder must either invent a branded-parameter surface the spec never names (e.g. a typed admission-construction helper in `producer-auth.ts`), or weaken S2 to target a `commissaire.ts`-internal type — and the PR ships a brand that provably erases at every real edge while the spec claims otherwise.

objections.claim: §3 requires `parseGovernedRecord` to construct records "field-by-field with runtime validation" whose `producer_id`/`contract_revision` are "typed plain `string`", **and** requires that "a malformed record still flows `deriveKey(master, undefined, …)` → HMAC mismatch" with no `null`→deny. These cannot both hold: if the pinned field type is `string` and the parser validates it, a record missing `producer_id` fails parsing — and the spec never says what happens then (returning `null` on the ledger read is exactly the `null`→deny path it forbids; skipping the record changes the failure surface). If the parser does not validate presence, the field type must be `string | undefined` (or optional), contradicting "typed plain `string`" — and under `strict`, passing it to a `string`-typed `deriveKey` parameter is a compile error. The spec pins the byte-for-byte outcome as a holdout AC (S8) while specifying a record type that cannot deliver it.
objections.evidence: §3 "Ledger-read fields stay plain `string`" items (1)–(3); S8 ("byte-for-byte: `deriveKey(master, undefined, …)` → HMAC mismatch, never a throw and never a `null`→deny divergence"); DONE bullet repeating both.
objections.predicted_consequence: The builder must silently deviate from the stated field type (make it optional) or from the parser contract (skip/reject malformed records), and one of those deviations fails S8 or S4a — the exact parity property the slice's central ratified resolution exists to protect.

objections.claim: The new enforcement control is specified by an exhaustive-sounding node list — "fail on any `AsExpression`/`TypeAssertionExpression`" — but TypeScript offers two further compile-time assertion forms that assert a type without a runtime check and are not in that list: the non-null assertion `value!` (a `NonNullExpression`, which asserts away `null`/`undefined` with no check — exactly the "unchecked cast crosses an input boundary" pattern the control exists to prohibit, e.g. `record.payload!.effect` on a parsed-`unknown` ledger record) and `expr satisfies T` (which can narrow for the checker without a cast node). A builder who hits a friction point with `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`/`noUncheckedIndexedAccess` on a boundary reader can reach for `!` and the check stays green while the guarantee the spec promises ("no unchecked cast crosses an input boundary") is silently hollow. Since the spec defines the control's enforcement surface by enumeration, the gap is in the spec, not a careless build.
objections.evidence: §3 "Boundary-contract check — Chosen": "fail on any `AsExpression`/`TypeAssertionExpression` (any target type, incl. `as any`/`as unknown` laundering)"; DONE item: "`scripts/check-no-boundary-cast.mjs` enforces three properties (no boundary cast of any target type; …)". No mention of `NonNullExpression` or `satisfies`.
objections.predicted_consequence: an unchecked non-null assertion on a validated-`unknown` boundary reader (e.g. a ledger payload field) passes the check and `tsc`, defeating the "no unchecked cast crosses an input boundary" principle on the auth path.

objections.claim: The entire slice is gated on content that the spec itself says is **not present** in the tree it will be built from — ADR-0132 and the FAFF-1168 spec must be on `main` @ `972ae4f6` before conversion starts, and the spec records that "the current `docs/v5-addendum-1` tree lacks them." A blocking dependency on unmerged upstream work is drawn as an *assumption* with a verify step, not as a sequenced dependency with a defined behaviour when it fails.
objections.evidence: §7 "Assumes (blocking pre-build gate): the build branches from `main` (ADR-0132 + FAFF-1168 spec live @ `972ae4f6`); the current `docs/v5-addendum-1` tree lacks them. `git show HEAD:records/adr/0132-…md` must succeed before conversion starts."
objections.predicted_consequence: If the build agent branches from the tree as it stands, the pre-build gate fails on the first command and the slice cannot start; nothing in the spec says what happens then (wait, cherry-pick, or proceed unratified), so the increment is not self-contained and shippable on its own.

objections.claim: `scripts/check-no-boundary-cast.mjs` is a self-contained new lint tool — a TS-compiler-API AST walker with its own planted-violation fixtures, three enforced properties, and a `node --test` leg. It is not the conversion; it is enforcement *of* the conversion, and it could land as its own increment after the `.ts` sources exist. Bundling it grows the PR's review surface (a compiler-API AST walker is exactly the kind of code that needs its own careful review) and couples the conversion's acceptance to a tool that does not need to ship with it.
objections.evidence: §3 "Boundary-contract check — Chosen. `scripts/check-no-boundary-cast.mjs` (TS-compiler-API AST walk, `node --test` leg) enforces three structural properties `tsc` alone cannot" + §4 step 4 + the DONE bullet for the checker.
objections.predicted_consequence: A single PR carrying a toolchain, two module conversions, a new AST-walking lint, a regions guard, and CI wiring — reviewable, but large enough that a defect in the checker (the newest, least-exercised code) delays or blocks landing the otherwise-independent conversion.

objections.claim: ADR-0132 is `Proposed`, and its status note says FAFF-1170 "is the acceptance that flips it, **or narrows it** if a real `tsc` emit surfaces a resolution wrinkle." Yet the spec's tsconfig and layout choices cite ADR-0132 as settled authority (layout (d), `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions` kept "per ADR-0132"). If the real conversion narrows the ADR, several "Chosen" toolchain decisions in this spec are the things being tested, not things already decided — the spec does not mark which toolchain choices are open to revision by the slice's own acceptance evidence.
objections.evidence: ADR-0132 "Status note: `Proposed`. FAFF-1170 … is the acceptance that flips it, or narrows it…"; spec §3 "Chosen: keep `rewriteRelativeImportExtensions` per ADR-0132" and the layout-(d) decisions.
objections.predicted_consequence: If the real `tsc` emit diverges from the hand-staged fixture (the exact wrinkle ADR-0132 defers to this slice), the agent has no spec-sanctioned room to adjust the layout/tsconfig without a re-review, because every relevant choice is marked `Chosen` on the authority of an unaccepted ADR.

objections.claim: The spec mandates boundary readers typed `unknown` feeding `parseGovernedRecord(raw): GovernedRecord | null`, but never states what `verifyAuthLeg`/`evaluateDecisionRequest` do with the `null` return — except for the single S8 case (malformed `producer_id`, which the spec pins to flow through to `deriveKey(master, undefined, …)` → `producer-auth-mismatch`). These two commitments are in tension: a field-by-field validator that "validates" `producer_id` as a string would naturally return `null` for a missing one, which is exactly the record S8 requires to reach `deriveKey` un-gated. A builder can resolve this several ways — parse-null records silently skipped (a malformed record vanishes from the auth leg instead of failing it), parse-null treated as a new failure reason, or parse never gating record bodies at all (null only for non-object garbage) — and each satisfies every named DONE item and scenario differently.
objections.evidence: §3 "Ledger-read fields stay plain `string`" ("Validate into pinned record types via `parseGovernedRecord(raw: unknown): GovernedRecord | null` … constructed field-by-field") vs. the same section's parity commitment ("a malformed record still flows `deriveKey(master, undefined, …)` → … `producer-auth-mismatch`") and S8. S8 decides only the malformed-`producer_id` shape; a record that fails `parseGovernedRecord` outright (e.g. non-object JSONL line, missing `seq`, wrong `schema`) has no specified outcome.
objections.predicted_consequence: Two builds both pass S8 and every DONE item yet diverge observably on whether a structurally-malformed ledger record is skipped silently or fails the auth leg — an audit-trail behavioural difference no named scenario can distinguish, and exactly the class of divergence the spec's own "CLI results unchanged" AC is meant to rule out.
